newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn to propose raising taxes on pensions.
newsitem.headline: Bonn to propose raising taxes on pensions.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said late on Tuesday the government's tax commission has agreed to raise taxes on pensioners with additional sources of income and will outline the proposal later this month.

Waigel declined to give any details as he spoke to reporters on the way out of a meeting between Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), Waigel's Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU) and the liberal Free Democrats (FDP).
FDP parliamentary leader Hermann Otto Solms said the commission's work was progressing well and the results of negotiations over a broad tax reform package would be made public on January 23.
The commission would propose increasing taxes on pensions, but the tax would be structured in such a way that most pensioners would remain unaffected, officials said.
Erwin Huber, Bavarian state finance minister and a member of the tax commission, told German radio that as much as 90 percent of pensioners had nothing to fear from the changes.
The tax increase on pensions would affect those with alternative income sources such as revenue from renting property or interest income.
The tax increase would be offset somewhat by a commensurate rise in tax deductions on pension insurance payments.
The tax commission will meet on Monday to discuss proposals for lowering German income tax rates.
Relations in the centre-right coalition of Kohl's alliance of CDU and the smaller CSU and the liberal Free Democrats have been strained over differences on how quickly to abolish the solidarity tax.

The tax is a 7.5-percent surcharge on income tax bills to finance German unification. It will fall to 5.5 percent next year. The FDP wants to abolish the tax all together, but the CDU and CSU said this would bust the budget.
Solms said the issue was not discussed at Tuesday's meeting.
